maya: Heads up — seeing a p95 latency regression (~12ms) on prefill-heavy flows after kernel-selector v2 rollout when prefix KV cache hit >= ~60%. Repro in staging (dedicated). Suspect interaction between softpad admission and kernel fallback. Logs + quick profile below.

ashwin: ugh. can you paste the p50/p95 numbers and which kernels were picked? :thinking_face:

maya: quick numbers from staging run (2026-03-17T22:10Z):
```
baseline (selector v1 -> kernel A8): p50=14ms p95=28ms tok/s=740
selector v2 (picked kernel B12 for many prefills when hit>=60%): p50=16ms p95=40ms tok/s=650
KV cache hit ~72% on that traffic slice
```

maya: profiler snippet (sampled wall times):
```
prefill: queue_wait=4ms softpad_copy=3ms kernel_select=2ms dispatch_wait=6ms kernel_exec=7ms
hot path overhead (selector + softpad): ~13ms added
```

jordan: that matches a trace I saw locally — kernel B12 disables the fused-KV fast-path for small prefill sequences, so prefill ends up going through a slower codepath even though KV hit is high. selector v2 is preferring B12 for memory/throughput reasons but loses on short-prefill latency.

oliver: quick thought: can we bias admission so cached-prefill requests avoid softpad (or prefer kernel A8) for short sequences? i can try a config toggle:
```
PATCH /configs/batcher
- admission.softpad.enabled = true
+ admission.softpad.enabled = true
+ admission.softpad.override_when.cached_prefix = false
```
(rough idea: opt-out softpad when request.metadata.cached_prefix == true)

maya: ran a 30m A/B: softpad-off for cached prefixes -> p95 drops from 40ms to ~30ms, p50 roughly unchanged. downside: packing efficiency drops a bit (cost +2%), and throughput dips on long tails.

ashwin: tradeoff makes sense. other idea: add a lightweight queue split instead of toggling softpad globally — keep cached-prefill in its own microqueue so kernel_selector sees more homogeneous batches and doesn't flip kernels mid-batch. also adjust token_budget_target down when hit_ratio high to avoid forcing kernel switch for a few tokens.

jordan: proposed policy (sketch):
- two admission queues: `cached_prefill` and `normal`
- `cached_prefill` target_token_budget = max(4, floor(avg_prefill_len/2))
- apply kernel_debounce: require 3 consecutive batches to prefer a different kernel before switching
- sampled trace emitted with `kernel_decision_reason` tag

ashwin: +1. the `kernel_debounce` is important — current selector flips on short statistical deltas and that triggers the softpad+kernel mismatch.

perf-bot: perf-bot: created perf-experiments/1749999999 with canary config and attached run-id=perf-1749999999-1

maya: I'll kick off a 6h canary in staging with the queue split + token_budget adjustment + kernel_debounce. dropping sampled traces into s3://redwood-perf/traces/1749999999 and enabling console flag `show_kernel_reason`. @ashwin can you help pick the initial magic numbers?

ashwin: on it. starting with token_budget=6 for cached_prefill, debounce=3 batches, emit 1/1000 sampled traces. will post results in this thread once first 2h buckets complete.

oliver: once we have canary results let's correlate with kernel-level perf counters (L2 miss, memcpy counts) — if B12 shows higher memcpy on small prefill we should change its short-prefill fast-path or add a micro-kernel for cached-prefill.

maya: noted. thanks all. will share the 2h snapshot around ~1750000000.

ashwin: quick note: added a console panel to annotate kernel switches per route so product folks can see impact. :eyes:
